claims.hypothesis: Radio continuum decrements exist under the scattered-light shadows of the DoAr 44 warped inner disc
claims.experiment: New ALMA Band 6 and Band 7 high resolution continuum imaging with MPolarMaps azimuthal profiles compared with SPHERE Q_phi(H)
claims.result: Dips found at PA 316.3/316.9 deg (north) and 152.9 deg (south), much shallower than in the IR
claims.finding: Radio decrements confirmed and nearly coincident in position with IR dips, but shifted clockwise

evidence.quote: We found intensity dips in the resolved ALMA imaging of the radio continuum, confirming the predictions from paper I.

claims.hypothesis: The IR dips are shadows from a misaligned inner disc
claims.experiment: Idealized geometrical model applied to the 2019 Q_phi(H) dip positions, and comparison with Paper I RT predictions
claims.result: xi = 21.4 +6.7/-8.3 deg; 2019 data matched by xi ~ 20 deg and 2016 data by xi ~ 30 deg
claims.finding: A misaligned inner disc explains the shadows, and its orientation appears to vary between epochs

evidence.quote: Geometrical models of $Q_{\phi}(H)$ provide support for a misaligned inner disc, with a relative inclination of $\xi$ = 21.4 $^{+6.7}_{-8.3}$ deg.

claims.hypothesis: The mm intensity dips are temperature decrements rather than optical depth changes
claims.experiment: Spectral index map between 230 and 350 GHz
claims.result: alpha ~ 2.0 +/- 0.1 along the ring with no distinct azimuthal variation at the dips
claims.finding: Emission is likely optically thick, so the dips are probably temperature decrements

evidence.quote: We do not find distinct azimuthal spectral variations in the location of the decrements

claims.hypothesis: The clockwise shift of radio decrements relative to IR dips is a thermal lag and constrains the gas surface density
claims.experiment: Thermal-lag T(phi) model with a_max = 1 cm, f_gd = 100, f = 1 applied to the measured shifts, assuming a retrograde outer disc
claims.result: Sigma_g = 117 +/- 10 g/cm2 (north, shift 14.95 deg) and 48 +/- 10 g/cm2 (south, shift 7.92 deg); contrast ratio f_r = 2.4 +/- 0.5
claims.finding: Shifts are consistent with a thermal lag for a retrograde disc, and a lopsided disc is also consistent with the large continuum crescent

evidence.quote: For a retrograde disc, such shifts are expected from a thermal lag

referee_caveats_inferred: The 21.4 deg relative inclination rests on one idealized geometrical model with an imperfect circular-ring and cavity-centre assumption; no independent fit of the SPHERE image with RT is done
Epoch-to-epoch SPHERE differences could be affected by observing conditions and the unresolved-polarisation subtraction, which the paper says moves the dip locations
The thermal-lag Sigma_g depends on assumed a_max, f_gd, f and a retrograde rotation, none of which are tested, and the uncertainty derivation is not explained
Radio dip contrasts are small (e.g. 98 percent, 83 percent of peak) and the paper gives only 1/10 beam-based errors on positions
Band 6 PA given as 59.9 in the text but 59.2 in Table 1
